title: Did you try to work with a publisher?
author: LeCosm0
selftext:
Hello!

Game dev here. I don't use AI to develop my games yet, but I'm interested in the technology. For now, we've decided not to use any AI in our games, aside from some coding support here and there. But I was wondering if any of you have already submitted a heavily AI-made game to a publisher (especially with art)?

If so:

* How did you choose which publisher to send it to?
* Did you check their stance on AI (even though very few have taken a clear position)?
* How did the discussion go?
* Did you manage to sign a publishing deal (even without funding)?

Let me know, I'm curious about your pioneer experience!

comments.author: drallcom3
comments.body:
AI aside and having worked with publishers from both sides I can tell you

- In the end they care about profits

- They're surprisingly bad at telling which game will make a profit

- They kind of invest in you, less so your game

- They love a good presentation

- Even more they love a game that they think is marketable. Publishing is all about marketing. That's also what you need them for.

- They get a shitload of presentations and even more AI slop

replies.author: LeCosm0
replies.body: I completely agree with all your points, but I still wonder how many of them would react to receiving a game that's clearly heavy on AI. Hooded Horse, for example, made a clear anti-AI statement, so I’m sure they wouldn’t appreciate it! 😅

replies.author: drallcom3
replies.body:
> but I still wonder how many of them would react to receiving a game that's clearly heavy on AI

Too many of them are too scared of Twitter opinions. I think we're still 2 years away from publishers fully accepting any form of AI.

replies.author: LeCosm0
replies.body: So the apprehension surrounding Twitter still outweighs their appetite for profit…

replies.author: Usam77
replies.body:
“Hooded Horse, for example, made a clear anti-AI statement, so I’m sure they wouldn’t appreciate it! 😅”


Your post above says:


“we've decided not to use any AI in our games, aside from some coding support here and there.”



If you really mean just occasional code assist and such, then I think you might be overreading policies directed at gen-AI content. See below for a quote:
reddit.com/r/SandustryGame/…/p2xdxsf


“Hi! Just to clarify -- our policy at Hooded Horse is no Gen AI content -- no artwork, writing, etc. This mirrors Steam's AI disclosure policy, where Steam specifies: "We are aware that many modern game development enviorments have ai powered tools built into them. Efficiency gains through the use of these tools is not the focus of this section." Disclosure is required for content, not for efficiency tools, as gen ai coding tools have become very common in game development. Although our own policy predates Steam's, I think their reasoning probably led them to the same line and for the same reasons we aren't concerned about efficiency tools, as they don't raise the same ethical or legal concerns as gen ai produced content (artwork, writing, etc) -- the thing we prohibit. So a dev who uses claude to say check their loops are working right in some script or something, that's not something either we or Steam cares about. And it's everywhere now with microsoft co-pilot and such.
That having been said, we would absolutely not publish a game that was 'vibe coded' -- these tools are only useful as a small part of a toolkit of a talented programmer. Anything vibe coded is going to be a terrible game (and that seems to be what OP is mistakenly arguing here).”

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: I've only put mine on [itch.io](http://itch.io) and it asked to add tags if it was made with AI and I did. That's as far as I've gotten with having to "declare" that I used AI.
